newsitem.title: UK: Northern Rock raises first half profits 10.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Northern Rock raises first half profits 10.2 pct.

text.p: The Northern Rock Building Society, which will be floated on the stock exchange in October as a bank, on Wednesday said it raised first half pre-tax profits 10.2 percent to 97 million pounds ($163 million).
Northern Rock said its assets grew by 13.6 percent to 14.6 billion pounds while net retail receipts were up a massive 75 percent on the same period last year to 531 million pounds.
The society said its plans to convert are on schedule with the expected flotation date still set for October 1.

Net lending stood at 794 million pounds giving an estimated UK net mortgage market share of seven percent. The society said signs of recovery have been seen in the housing market, especially in the South East of England but activity in the first half was reduced overall, it said.
Northern Rock managing director Leo Finn said interest rate uncertainty with competition intensifying as large mortgage market players returned to the market after their flotations.

The society said it would sell its small Northern Rock Asset management unit and close Northern Rock Financial Services over the next twelve months, "as part of its strategic withdrawal from the provision of financial services."
- Joe Ortiz, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8864. ($ = 0.595 British Pounds)
